item.title: Echos eines Hoffest
item.description: A city returns to medieval times for a day. Foundation intervenes and it becomes permanent.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): History

Page Layout (Optional): Video logs, interviews, document references and incident logs to be included.

Elevator Pitch: The city of Mainz (Germany) gathers annually during the Pentecost day for a party in which the citizens anomalously change their behaviour as if they were in the 12th century for a day. After an incident, the Foundation intervenes only to provoke this change to become permanent.

Central Narrative: During the Pentecost day in Mainz, its citizens celebrate the festivity in a nearby location, where upon access they show an altered behaviour proper of the European nobility in the 12th century, such as a firm code of honour; and participate in joust tournaments. By the following day, citizens involved have no related memories.

+ Show
- Hide

This activity went under the radar of the Foundation until a Turkish attendant was found dead after one of these events with the words "Deus Vult" engraved on his chest. The following year, Foundation found out about these effects with on-site live-recordings. Identifying a potential assault similar to the previous year, a task force bursts into the gathering, disbanding all attendants. This time affected individuals keep their memories and the behaviour displayed during this event. Chaos ensues due to the cultural clash with modern Germany.

The next Pentecost day, affected population gathers again, live-recordings showing that the activities performed are exactly the same as in the previous year. Once the celebration finishes, all attendants return to the normal behaviour. Foundation decides not to interrupt this event, but stops population from attending by fencing the site. Instead, attendants move to nearby Ingelheim, where anomalous natural catastrophes result in hundreds of casualties. The Foundation allows the event to occur at the usual location, however impeding the attendance to vulnerable individuals.

Recording logs interview seemingly a monk, who seems to be responsible of these events. Back in 1184, Kaiser Barbarossa hosted a huge fest in that same location. By law, Konrad was to be seated by the Kaiser during the ceremonies, however he was substituted in a political move by the Archbishop of Cologne. Resentful, he condemned the dishonour, ensuring that that day would be repeated over and over until the Kaiser rectified his mistake.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This is a story about timely cultural clash, by bringing a huge population from the past to the current days. It is also a story about resentment and, literally, holding a grudge.

Additional Notes: Based on the 1184 Mainzer Hoftag. Kaiser Barbarossa might be SCP-125-DE.

Users will continue to float until they either hit a ceiling or the oil gets washed off. Upon hitting a ceiling or a limit, the user oil will continue to rise until it is off the user, where it'll then fall. The user will too fall due to the oil being removed.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX causes user's to controllably levitate upwards, people who consume SCP-XXXX will continually float upwards until they hit a ceiling. If the user continues to float upwards, they will eventually extricate it outwards, causing the user and the extrication to fall. If people who have consumed SCP-XXXX hit a limiter or a ceiling, they will be pulled up forcefully until their organs containing the oil rupture out of the consumer. causing the user to fall.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: SCP-XXXX is seemingly safe, but due to the container continuing to fill it's environment, it could cause the end of our known universe.

item.title: Storm of crows
item.description: SCP-XXXX is an anomalous phenomenon where an abnormal number of crows migrate directly to the town, even if it off-tracks their intended migration path.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is an anomalous phenomenon in Basney, Connecticut (a fictional town), where an abnormal number of crows migrate directly to the town, even if it off-tracks their intended migration path.

More
Not more

The highest record of crows at one point in the town was 84,784 crows (for reference, the town has a population of 1,812).
When a house in the town is damaged, it will start to heal by regeneration, although minor damages take less time to heal than major damages. Damages won't be healed as an identical version of the house, leaving flaws, such as furniture that was never there, irregular wallpaper patterns, doors or stairs leading to nothing, rooms or objects with irregular shape/or proportions, etc.

A unique crow will be "assigned" to a specific house in the town for every house. These crows are distinguishable by their single white feather. These crows (nicknamed "Protector Crows") will interact with the occupants of the homes they are assigned to, showing more compassion and intelligence than an average crow.

These crows are also the first sign that the anomalous phenomenon that is SCP-XXXX (the massive crow migration) is about to happen.

However, the foundation discovered that when a crow is killed, the house's self-repairing is assigned to stops entirely.

The foundation only knows what they get from observing the crows and testing, not really caring about anything other than keeping secrecy. So the story comes.

Central Narrative: The narrative is presented in a personal journal belonging to a young teenage girl named Sahra, who has lived in the town her whole life but will be in the first instance of SCP_XXXX. She lives with her parents and little sister, Rosa, and little brother, Eric.

more
not more

Keep in mind I'm going over the most important parts.

Their protector, crow, come to their house. Rosa names them Chip because they brought a corn chip as a gift to their windowsill.

The next day when Sahra goes to school, she notes that there are usually some crows in this town, but not this much. The crow population now is around 142.

Soon a large and irregular migration of crows to the town is detected by the local news. The town tries to find a way to scare off the crows. But none of their methods are working as every time one crow leaves, more come in replacement.

Sarah's dad one day breaks a door hinge while slamming a door shut. He later calls one of his friends to help fix it when he gets back home, but it's fixed when they get back home.

Soon the crows outnumber the town's population 12 to 1. Sarah mistakes a large number of crows on a tree as leaves, as a way to show how many of them there are.

The town tries to find a way to scare off the crows. They use fireworks, predators, big hunting, but none of them work as every time one goes away, more come to replace it. Soon the crow's number in the thousands.

One day a car crashes into Sarah's house and injures chip. They find chip dead, and the part the car hit started rapidly attempting to fix itself. The broken part starts to start to expand in size and uses the wrong building materials (like concrete for a door, plastic for the grade door, and even flesh). the crow's brain essentially went on overdrive mode right before dying, irregularly snd rapidly fixing any damaged parts. This is when the foundation is informed of something majorly anomalous happening.

The foundation came to the town, amnesticize everybody, move them out, create a cover story as to why there were so many crows, and find Sarah's journal.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: An article with a light story isn't as common as Lovecraftian horror and Apollyon class SCPs. And if you're looking for some big answer about why the crows go there or a dark secret about the town, you're missing the point.

Additional Notes: Sarah and her family were in the first instance of SCP-XXXX which is why the foundation hadn't known about the anomaly. I am still hoping to expand on the idea so any criticism will help.

item.title: Psychological Theories in 1800s
item.description: For a therapy SCP who was originally trained in the 1800s, what theories and practices would they most likely adhere to had they been trained around this time?
item.content:encoded:
This SCP is a reality-affecting entity that was captured by an English Earl (or baron, I'm unsure) at some point in the 1800s, probably around 1850 or later. I think the upper limit should probably be 1900 when the British nobility was dying off.

The earl in question had an interest in Psychology, and when he captured the anomalous entity he realised it's potential to help cure his patients. He slowly reformed the entity over time to genuinely come to enjoy helping humans, and it continued when he died.

A problem is is that the SCP mostly focuses on Therapeutic techniques, which from what i can gather came about more when Freud entered onto the scene, which i think was 1880 or so, which is a little early i think. It is also set in Britain, so it would be whatever theories were popular there.

So I'm currently unsure what theories of treatment this entity may subscribe to, as it would depend on which theories were around when it was being trained under this earl.

item.title: De Facto
item.description: An octopus that exploits laws of reality to actively shape the environment however it sees fit.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article
Genre: Horror

Elevator Pitch: De Facto is an intangible entity that can descend upon any location and transmute it to develop anomalous properties. It presents cephalopodic features and primarily resides outside of our reality, traveling freely along or through any surface and molding the environment into its personal hunting grounds.

Central Narrative:
+ Show
Hide Section

This creature was originally a rare variant of octopi possessing intelligence that far surpasses humans held in a secret underground marine biology laboratory. It preferred behavior often associated with its species, though can devise incredibly elaborate traps for anything it considers its prey, and adapts to immediate surroundings astonishingly fast. Its kind has been critically endangered due to human pollution and influence and retained a grudge over transgressions of its captors.

However, it eventually learned how it could adapt into reality itself and extend beyond the third dimension. It turned the entire containment facility into its personal den, transmuting the walls with an ink-coated rocky surface, restructuring the layout entirely as a system of dugouts and labyrinthian corridors, and filling various areas in an oily, repugnant ooze. Its now-countless tendrils sprawled visibly along the wall surfaces like projections, with all attempts to interfere with them showing no effect on the creature. Unnatural and anomalous phenomenon began to sprout in the twisted den: coral discharging suspended bubbles of ooze, manmade objects now malleably autonomous and extremely hostile to humans, and unspeakably horrific marine life that freely live and move through the air as if it was water.

The octopus started cornering each member of the facility’s personnel separately from each other, torturing them with whatever sadistic and anomalous means it could fabricate inside the burrows of its new home. Eventually, one by one each researcher would observe a large contorted beak emerge from the ink-black walls and gruesomely devour them, leaving enough space in the walls for everyone to hear sounds of their coworkers’ screams echo through the halls. It takes its leave when it’s finished, retracting its tentacles and ascending to the surface in search for more prey.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The creature practically infects any area with its anomalous properties, permanently transforming any building or structure into a waking nightmare.

Tags: adaptable, amorphous, animal, building, carnivorous, cephalopodic, hostile, intangible, keter, predatory, sentient, transfiguration

item.title: I'd Rather Be Part of the Serpent's Hand Than the Foundation"
item.description: I would be going, "SCREW THE FOUNDATION, YO! DOWN WITH THOSE GOSHDARN JAILORS!"
item.content:encoded:
So, I think the Serpent's Hand would be better to be a part of / work for than the SCP Foundation. Here are all my points, in no particular order:

1. Foundation operates out of boringly-decorated, overly sanitary-looking research facilities filled with deadly monsters that can get loose at any second, not to mention they are constantly raided by the Chaos Insurgency. The Serpent's Hand gets a frikin' extradimensional library that requires actual frikin' magic to access, and is actually very safe because all of the anomalies within are friendly as long as nobody gets violent against them or breaks the rules. Nice place to chill and relax, maybe play some Dungeons and Dragons and write in peace.

2. Foundation deprives anomalous humans of their humanity, and instead locks them up in basically prison (I don't give a crap about how much you think Iris Thompson likes it there, she most likely secretly hates being locked up, along with literally any other human SCP).

3. They fight for the rights of law-abiding anomalous humans that just want to go about their lives without having to worry about being either imprisonated by the SCP Foundation, murdered by the Global Occult Coalition, weaponized by the Chaos Insurgency, or sold by MC&D. Basically, they tell everybody else to chill their heels and leave anomalous people the heck alone. Which is actually a pretty noble cause. The only reason they raid Foundation / GoC locations is because that is one of the only ways to get their points across. Plus, they do stealth missions, and kill Foundation personnel in only a limited capacity.

4. The Serpent's Hand doesn't breach dangerous anomalies for no good reason at all. That's the Chaos Insurgency's job, after all. If the Serpent's Hand doesn't have a good reason to breach any given SCP during a raid, they won't breach said SCP. They do, however, steal Safe SCP items, and let peaceful human SCPs to escape. They may even attempt to free D-class if possible. They're not stupid, and they don't want to bring about the end of the world by releasing highly dangerous Euclid, Keter, and Apollyon SCPs. Again, that is the Chaos Insurgency's job.

5. Simply existing as a worker on a Foundation site means that you are alive on moment, and then the next you are dead due to being freakin' eaten by a massive lizard that is literally too angry to die or turned into a zombie by a dude cosplaying as a medieval plague doctor, and your friends and family will be unaware of your death (if all of them are outside of the foundation, which is most likely). If you do manage to survive through the containment breach, you will still be mentally scarred by the experience. As I said earlier, the Serpent's Hand operates out of a peaceful library, with a 0% chance of being eaten by a bloodthirsty monster.

6. I also believe that the serpent's hand probably is one of the morally better GoIs, considering their entire mission statement is "we want rights for anomalous humans, and knowledge about the paranormal should be public." While they do break the law from time to time (which would make them Chaotic or Neutral Good), they don't do so for no reason at all. They just want the world to be a better place.

item.title: The Drag Strip Phantom/The Black Magnum [Seeking Greenlight]
item.description: An SCP heavily and very directly inspired by Christine, The Wraith, Death Proof and SLR:Redline.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery/Thriller

Page Layout (Optional): Standard description and event chronology as well as mission reports and test logs

Elevator Pitch: The phantom of a car that manifests itself on lonely stretches of desert road at night to challenge high-performance passer-by cars to a drag race. Original manifestation is 1970 Camaro, however the list will expand later.

Central Narrative: A rumor spreads in a small town in Colorado about a mysterious "ghost car", originating from a local drag racing enthusiast. According to the legend, the racer is overtaken by a dragster and the road eventually leads into a foggy, abandoned drag strip - with a stoplight and everything. The Foundation takes note after several others report the same occurence and dispatches a team to study the anomaly up-close and personal ("prodding" the car during manifestations and exploring the strip dimension), as well as launching an investigation into the car's possible origins. At one point, a GoI destroys it (no clue which one yet); after which, basically, Christine happens: Someone finds a junk 1970 Camaro, and with maniacal passion restores it, builds it and, in the end, crashes it violently, dying - thus causing the phantom to be "reborn". Following rediscovery the Foundation tries to relocate it to the most discreet stretch of blacktop possible and keep it happy by regularly setting up drag races.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The mystery surrounding the car itself: Is it sentient, is it dangerous, what is the drag strip, is/was it a real place, where does the car come from, is there anyone driving it, what is its driving force etc. etc.

Additional Notes: The drag strip is a separate dimension that flat-out disables digital and some complex electronic devices./Cars cannot leave the dimension unless they engage in the race or get totaled./Anyone who dies on the strip in a car becomes another manifestation./The phantoms are free to switch or modify their vessels - however can only do so by leaving their old vessel in the real world or possessing somebody to do it, respectively./The phantom sustains itself off of life energy gained in the final stage of its "rebirth"./Each phantom is sentient and has a memory beyond its current vessel./The SCP can manifest at will anytime between sunset and dawn./It is not bound to any road in particular and can move at any time.

P.S. Apologies to everyone who got my email with no subject, I was very concentrated on getting outreach first
P.P.S. Apologies for the title being somewhat inconsistent with the idea, I posted this on accident when I wasn't done yet and constantly reedited it.

item.title: The burger that steals your emotions. (Seeking Greenlight)

item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: To boil it down to the basics, a higher society of beings created an engine that fuels off of negative emotions and stimuli. They found that humans generate a certain type of particle, that gives off an immense amount of energy. They made it the center of their lives and their planet's ecosystem. However concealing a giant engine is difficult, so they hid it within a pocket dimension. The entrance of which is a fast-food restaurant. Those entering find themselves transported to the engine, disguised as the restaurant. And if certain "cogs" of the engine escape to our world, they explode. Spectacularly.

item.title: Questions about SCP Content on Twitch.tv and more
item.description: I want to create a Twitch Channel based on a SCP Article
item.content:encoded:
Hey! I recently came up with an idea for a SCP Article and Concept that I don't think has ever been done before and isn't really covered in the wiki's legal guidelines.

Essentially I want to create a VTuber (Virtual YouTuber or Twitch Streamer) to stream on Twitch with. VTuber's are generally 3D models that are rigged to react to the operator's movements and emotions. I wanted to create one based off of a SCP article (That i am currently writing) which would be useed as his backstory.

For more information on the Concept: VTuber SCP Concept

So…. I have a lot of questions…

Questions about Twitch Licensing and Credits:
1. Since the Character I would be streaming as is based on a SCP Article which falls under SCPwiki’s CC Licensing, I would assume the content I produce would need to fall under that same License? If so, I'm not sure how to set that up with twitch as I'm not entirely sure what their content falls under.

2. With the Character being an original creation of mine, would I still need to link to it’s article page and the Author (Me) for credit? Or would just linking to the SCPwiki be sufficient?

3. What rules and/or limitations (if any) would I need to abide by in my content since twitch is an Offsite platform? Examples: 1. Would I be able to stream myself as this character playing a game? even though the game may fall under a different license than CC? 2. As a musician, would I be able to cover copyrighted songs? (provided I follow twitch’s guidelines concerning music as well)

Questions about the Model:
I created the Model and Name before I had the idea to make it a SCP. In that case, would the model (including related images) and name still belong to me, but just be used on the wiki and on stream with my permission? Or would the model and name need to be under CC as well?

Not all of the content being producing would be directly related to the SCP universe, but if the character is connected, I'm not sure what limitations and restrictions would be applied

I love the SCP Universe and don't want to do anything that would be against their guidelines, nor do I want to incur the wrath of a DMCA Take down.

In closing I have no idea what I am doing lol, and any legal help or advice is extremely appreciated!

(There are probably many things that I have not thought of and many questions may rise up. if you have any questions or suggestions of other questions I should be asking, please let me know)

Man, when I first discovered scp, i was awful at writing. At the best of times you'd get an incoherent mess that completely defied things such as tone, theme, plot, and grammar. Now, if I sit down and write a story, it will at least make sense grammatically.

I mean, in my head i can craft a coherent story, but ideas don't mean [REDACTED] to be honest, the biggest struggle I've faced when joining the scp community, (aside from biting the bullet and dealing with the garbage interface that is wikidot) has been coming up with an idea I'm ok with throwing into the kindling. By that, I mean an idea which i don't think i could expand upon further when i improve in skill.

It's difficult to find someone who shares my struggle. I don't suffer from a lack of ideas. I don't suffer from a lack of effort. I struggle from being to picky. I have a plethora of ideas I wish to spew upon paper, but I just don't feel I'm sufficiently skilled enough to do them justice.

And I'm stuck in this purgatory of coming up with an idea that I'm ok with letting go of. I have so many ideas for scp as a whole, not just anomalous objects, I'm talking tales, GOI's, canons, and so much more. I guess I'm just frustrated that I'm not confident enough in my skull to allow myself to write what I want.

item.title: The Friendly Shadow
item.description: Clarence's Shadow is alive, sentient, and his best friend.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Emotional

Elevator Pitch: A sentient, living shadow, who belongs to a man named Clarence.

+ The Friendly Shadow's Quirk Ideas
- Close

Whether these are a good ideas or not is why I'm putting these here. Yell out if any seem good or bad. I always like to hear feedback and opinions.

  1. I was thinking that the shadow could move off of Clarence and interact with other shadows of people and objects. When the shadow interacts with any other shadow, object or person, he can move it as he can interact with it just like any other person could with psychical objects. If he picks up the shadow of a remote, it will float above the spot he is holding it. If he pats someone's shadow on the back, the physical person will feel the same effect. He can do this off and on Clarence.
  2. The shadow can only talk to people through charades. It doesn't have a physical mouth, so it can't talk.

Central Narrative: It revolves around the wholesome relationship between Clarence and his Shadow.

+ Expanding on the Narrative
- Close

I'm hoping to let this be emotional. I want a rather wholesome attachment with Clarence and his shadow. They have known of each other since childhood. It's not some recent anomaly. They've been best friends for life, sharing each other accomplishments, laughing together, and working together. Even if Shadow's accomplishments are more private and hidden to onlookers.
The big twist is that Clarence is created by the shadow. This being why it's not some recent anomaly and why the Foundation can't find any link to Clarence's family. This will be unfolded in the Addendum.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Clarence was made by the Shadow. As a friend and a mobile person to keep attached too and see the world.

Additional Notes:

+ The Inspiration
- Close

For those who are as nerdy as me, the inspiration behind this was three things specifically.

  1. The Movie which has yet to (or may never) be released, Me and My Shadow. Note: If you've seen or are about to look up what this is, you'll know this had the biggest impact of the three.
  2. Peter Pan and his shadow
  3. Doctor Who, Season 4, Episode 8, Silence in the Library.

Let me know what can be used (if anything can be). Can't wait to hear from you. -Cope

Thanks Blazer. - Cope

item.title: The Mushroom Men
item.description: A sentient and talented species of fungus and the funerary cave in their charge, their lifestyle, history, territory, uses and peril...
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional):

Page Layout (Optional):

Elevator Pitch: A tribe of sentient fungus people clawing out a living on the edge of the Lake Bikal Secure Containment Zone…

  • See the funerary cave they maintain and a peculiar stone age corpse within, deformed from a long, losing battle against SCP 610. (I do have a mystery for this in mind, but i'm not spoiling it.)
  • Hear of their mycelial network, like a brain unto itself in complexity, capable of healing, administering medications and poisons, and communicating directly with the land itself.
  • Their reproduction is slowed by climate change drying out the soil they live in and leaching it of nutrients. The permafrost is melting, the warm temperatures and drier weather are slowly killing them. If the Foundation doesn't take drastic measures to preserve them they'll go extinct in less than a century. Worse, its believed they keep the terraforming effects of SCP 610 in check. Without them, future 610 breaches will probably cause much more damage.

*I'm working on an ongoing connected series of articles and a story shared between them with conservation being the underlying thread. This is part of that.

Central Narrative: A more ecologically based view of the OG Sarkic Anomaly, the amazing environmental flexibility of fungi and their age old conflict with bacteria, musings of what a sentient mushroom might look like, and whether there really is a separation between flesh, nature, and machine.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Loosely inspired by a cave painting and the work of Professor Paul Stamets. I tried to capture the uses and habits of fungi and their importance to the environment in an SCP, from the best known to the theoretical. They also pose a different kind of breach risk to the Foundation, one I attempted to base on real life concerns over the human consequences of climate change.

Additional Notes: OMG I did it! A proposal that expresses everything I wanted to in less than 400 words!!!!!

item.title: SCP Idea: Aggressive Earworm (Seeking Greenlight)
item.description: Mediocre copyright-free music as anart
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Comedy, Drama

Page Layout: Standard article with a set of media players, multiple updates/addenda.

Elevator Pitch:

+ show block
– hide block

Generic copyright free music is anart created to replace all other music. The SCP is an 'album' of several similar songs created as a protest of music censorship, following the "If I can't have it, nobody can" trope. The songs are all slightly different, but are recognized by the presence of Ukulele, Glockenspiel, Whistling, and Rhythmic Clapping. The music has anomalous effects following these rough stages:
1. Listeners can't get the song 'out of their head', and find themselves compelled to hum/play along. They begin to prefer the anomalous music over other kinds.
2. The anomalous music begins to replace other music affected people listen to. They feel compelled to spread the anomalous music through playing it in public or using it as background music in other media.
3. All sounds begin to sound like the music to affected people, they can no longer speak without singing the tune.
These effects are felt most strongly/rapidly by musicians, artists, or other 'creative' types.

Central Narrative:

+ show block
– hide block

The music is primarily spread online, with the creator uploading the music to various music sharing/streaming sites. The Foundation is notified to its existence when news of 'undeletable songs' start appearing in online music forums. By the time they track down the source and start to counteract the anomalous music the original artist disappears/escapes, and the music continues to be posted in new locations. The spread is contained through intensive screening of streaming sites, and forced editing to remove anomalous frequency patterns from the music and disable its effects in places where it cannot be otherwise removed outright. They believe that they've achieved stable containment when the worsening effects of the anomaly begin to emerge in those already affected. Cue test logs to show someone deafening themselves and/or communicating through writing to try and mitigate the effects. The effects are only curable through intensive Amnestic treatment, however exposure to the non-anomalous versions of the music can still cause relapse.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

+ show block
– hide block

An artist is upset at the misuse and illegal sharing of their own work and create a song to intentionally destroy all musical creativity. Due to the widespread use of similar music in the real world, and recent frustrations over DMCA takedowns and copyright 'being broken' the reader will likely be familiar with both the music and the feelings of frustration around it, showing how far the SCP has 'already' spread.

Edit: Added clarifications and collapsibles, thank you Zyn.

item.title: Reality Warping Anime Husbando VTuber (Seeking Greenlight)
item.description: I want to create an actual VTuber based in the SCP Universe
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article/Joke SCP

Genre (Optional): Other (Meta)

Page Layout (Optional): Description and Containment Article

Elevator Pitch: Reality Warper who can digitally transfer his consciousness through various realities, and as a result becomes a Virtual Tuber "VTuber" in our reality.

Central Narrative: Due to being cast out from his body in a containment attempt by the foundation, His consciousness created a virtual body in our reality, Where he has learned extensively about the Foundation through the Wiki. Though originally classified as safe, the foundation reclassified him as Euclid due to the potential of Memetic SCP Containment breaches and broken masquerade situations. He is aware that the SCP Universe is considered Fictional in our reality and has used this to learn as much about it as he can.

+ show block
– hide block

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It's an Anomalous VTuber, which (hopefully) will also have a real life presence on twitch, making it Unique, Interesting, and Interactive

Additional Notes: I am not entirely sure how an idea such as this would fit into the SCP Universe, nor how I should write it exactly. I would love any suggestions or input on the functional application of this concept.

As mentioned above, I have full intention of turning this concept into an actual VTuber on Twitch, which brings in another side of this which I don't believe has ever been done before. It also raises a question about the ethical nature such a concept, since VTubers and streamers often make money on their platforms, and the SCP universe being in a strange gray area concerning copyright and monetization. Due to the nature of such platforms, the actual SCP content would not be directly monetized, but I'm curious to hear other peoples thoughts on this topic.

Just to be clear, I am not doing this in hopes of launching a VTuber career off the back of the SCP universe. I had planned on Creating a VTuber for awhile now and was trying to come up with an interesting backstory. This just kind of clicked for me, though it would just be the backstory and may not actually contribute to the active stream very often. It will be a variety stream of music, gaming and other activities.

Monetization is not the goal, I just wanted to create a cool character and expose people to 2 communities that I love. (VTubers and The SCP Foundation).

item.title: The Three Sided Coin (revised)
item.description: A 3 sided coin that turns men into monsters, both figuratively and literally. [thread locked, repeat]
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Humerous Horror

Page Layout: A fairly standard SCP article layout with an interview log and an addendum at the end.

Elevator Pitch

  • Its an anomalous coin that will reveal 3 different sides when flipped over. The 3rd side is anomalous.
  • When the coin lands on the 3rd side it transforms whoever flipped it into a monster.
  • In addition if someone keeps the coin for a long time it will alter their behavior, making them kinda crazy but in a fun way.

Central Narrative: The foundation learns about a weird death in Las Vegas and finds a man named Mr. Exolia in police custody. He has a "magic coin" and after losing a bet with a foundation agent agrees to come in willingly. While detained he has some humorous antics in an interview. Eventually a test is done where he gambles with a D-class and then transforms into the monster and kills the D-class. The coin is then taken from him and he goes into withdraw symptoms. He's eventually given amnestics and released to witness protection. The coin is kept at a foundation site until it is stolen by a custodian.

Hook: Mr. Exolia's humorous yet dangerous nature. He is quick witted and funny, but also clearly is trying to trick people into making bets with him that could potentially get them killed.

Notes: This is a revised version of my first thread. Hopefully this one makes a little more sense.

item.title: Extreme Larping (seeking greenlight)
item.description: Character sheets for an RPG that extends beyond the tabletop.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes or No

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Comedy / Action

Page Layout (Optional): Article, with Incident Reports and Experiment Logs

Elevator Pitch: Premade TTRPG character sheets that cause users to become the characters used on them, abilities and all — but they're still constrained by game rules and dice. They literally produce dice and roll them, and the effects happen in the real world.

Central Narrative: The discovery section follows a group of friends who found the sheets online, used them in a game, and then started exhibiting anomalous properties as a result. Some are killed during an attempt at containment as a fight plays out between an MTF squad and the characters, surviving characters are contained and characters from different classes are subject to foundation experiments; multiple containment breaches result from the unpredictable breadth of the characters' abilities, and the catastrophic nature of "Crits" on ability checks.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: An affected individual might "Roll Stealth" poorly when trying to escape containment — literally producing and rolling a d20, and then intentionally throw itself back into custody on a 1. Alternatively, they may succeed at escaping despite overwhelming odds on a 20.

They also appear to "level up" and gain new traits after "encounters" with foundation security — leading each subsequent breach to be more severe. One or more of the characters reaching max level could result in an upgrade to Keter class or even an XK class scenario.

Additional Notes: It's unclear what happened to the Dungeon Master of the initial game, or how stats for real entities and objects are determined.

item.title: What's the Purpose of a Nightmare? (seeking greenlight)
item.description: A projector that can make cartoons out of dreams
item.content:encoded:
A projector that can make cartoons out of dreams seems fun at first, but sharing a nightmare can have devastating consequences.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlight: Yes

SCP Article

Page layout: The SCP file, and then a section which security clearance is needed to access, which details the events that happened involving the SCP.

Elevator Pitch: A projector that makes dreams into cartoons. When someones night terror is projected, it turns into a memetic SCP that tortures people in their dreams.

Central narrative: A researcher named Dr.Summers is assigned to stop the memetic scp from spreading. She keeps a log of her efforts. She manages to suppress the infected and isolate them all, but she herself gets infected in the process. She then desprately tries to find out how to undo it, while the torture in the dreams becomes so surreal and brutal that victims start killing themselves rather than experience it. She takes a ton of anti-sleep meds and manages to figure out that having an infected's dreams projected and watched by an uninfected viewer will pass the infection to them.

+ show block
– hide block

She manages to save the remaining researchers and staff by transmitting their infections to D-class, but she herself is apprehensive because it turns out that not sleeping for a long times will make the experience in the dream exponentially worse. She finally does it, and has a conversation with the nightmare entity in the dream about it's motives. (it manifested from the nightmares of a D-class with a lot of anxiety over their eventual fate, and now it wants to impress that feeling on everyone else at the site.) It prepares to put her through an experience her mind couldn't survive, but since dr.summers is a lucid dreamer she manages to overpower it's control over the dream just long enough to display the "the end" screen that appears on all the cartoons the scp produces. This ends the dream, and she manages to escape with her sanity intact. The report ends with an addendum saying that she figured out the meme spread by people telling others about their dreams, so she'll have to hide most of her report as classified information, and she hopes no one reads it in the future. (the reader just read the whole thing).

Hook: I think it's a fun creepy story and premise, and I have ideas for a lot of fun visuals to include with it.
